Kettering Health participates in the federal 340B Drug Pricing Program as part of its commitment to improving the health and well-being of the communities it serves. The program allows eligible Kettering Health entities to purchase outpatient medications at reduced prices, generating savings that are reinvested to expand access to care, improve affordability, and strengthen patient services.

Consistent with federal guidance, 340B savings are not maintained as a separate fund but are integrated into the overall financial framework of Kettering Health. These resources are strategically deployed to directly support patient care initiatives, particularly for underserved, uninsured, and underinsured populations.

Kettering Health uses 340B program savings to broaden access to essential healthcare services. These resources help offset the significant financial burden reflected in the $376.5 million in uncompensated care provided in 2025, enabling:

Expansion of services in rural and underserved communities
Sustainability of critical programs that operate at a financial loss
Medication affordability remains a central focus of Kettering Health’s 340B strategy. The 2025 data reflect a comprehensive approach that includes:
Direct financial assistance to reduce patient out-of-pocket costs
Free drug replacement programs ensuring continuity of therapy
Copay support for high-cost infusion and specialty medications
Innovative tools such as the 340B Care Card program
These efforts reduce financial barriers and complement the system’s broader charity care and uncompensated care commitments.
The breadth of assistance across infusion, specialty, and ambulatory care settings reflects Kettering Health’s investment in comprehensive clinical services. 340B savings help support:
Advanced therapies for complex and chronic conditions
Specialty pharmacy management of high-cost medications
These services are essential in managing the needs of patients who may otherwise contribute to uncompensated care if access were limited.

Kettering Health recognizes that financial hardship is a major barrier to care. The combination of $91.8 million in patient assistance and $376.5 million in uncompensated care demonstrates a system-wide commitment to reducing these barriers.
Additional support includes transportation, education, and care coordination services that ensure patients can access and adhere to treatment.
Delivering this level of patient and community support requires significant operational investment. 340B savings fund:
Clinical pharmacy teams and patient assistance coordinators
Infrastructure supporting specialty and infusion services
Technology systems for tracking and optimizing assistance
